title: desksupervise-status-v1 runtime snapshot
description: Machine-readable contract for the JSON document `desksupervise status --json` emits: the liveness observer's per-claim runtime state as one structured record, so a console can consume it without reading Go. Every field follows the three-state-instrument rule (docs/three-state-instrument-rule.md): an unreadable or not-applicable source renders `n/a` (durations, timestamps), `could-not-check` (the `resource` block's fields), or `null` (a `resource` field the reporting session left unset this tick) — never a default zero. `tokens` used to be a permanently could-not-check stub at the claim level; a later revision (example-stream/13) fills that binding by moving it into `resource`, a self-reported vitals block joined from the claim holder's own roster beacon (tokens, context-% used, session age, subagent count, model) — still three-state throughout, and a measured 0 is a legitimate reading that must never be read as "unknown". The human table `desksupervise status` (without --json) is NOT a contract and is not described here.

schema.description: The schema marker; exactly desksupervise-status-v1 for this contract.

now.description: The RFC3339 clock the snapshot was evaluated at (the --now override under fixtures, else the real clock).

claims.description: One entry per in-flight claim rendered (all in-flight claims, or — under --stops — only those carrying an armed stop).

repo.description: owner/name of the repo the claim lives on.

item.description: The item id the claim covers.

holder.description: The session/owner holding the claim, or n/a.

claimed_at.description: RFC3339 acquisition time, or n/a when unknown.

last_observed_at.description: RFC3339 most-recent sign of life, or n/a when none/blind.

observed_via.description: The source that last observed the worker, or n/a.

liveness.description: The liveness taxonomy verdict (loopengine.ClassifyLiveness), or COULD-NOT-CHECK when the probes could not be read.

timers.description: Remaining time on each of the three liveness timers; each a Go duration string (e.g. 5m0s) or n/a when the timer does not apply to this claim's phase, its policy knob is disabled, or the claim is blind. A blind claim NEVER renders 0s.

stop.description: The stop armed for this claim/item, or null when none is armed. Distinct from a global STOP flag, which halts the whole desk before status runs.

armed_at.description: RFC3339 time the stop was armed, or n/a.

resource.description: Self-reported vitals from the claim's holder session (example-stream/13): tokens burned, percent of the context window used, session age, subagents spawned, and the model id. Only the session itself can know these — they are joined from its own roster beacon (deskkit's MergeResourceVitals write). Each field is three-state: a measured value, the string could-not-check (no readable beacon for the holder, or the session's own read of that source failed), or null (the reporting session's emitter simply left the field unset this tick). A measured 0 is a legitimate reading and is never rendered as could-not-check or dropped to null.

tokens.description: Cumulative tokens the session has consumed.

context_pct_used.description: Percent of the context window in use, 0-100.

session_age_seconds.description: Wall seconds since the session booted.

subagents_spawned.description: Count of subagents this session has launched.

model.description: The model id the session runs.

aggregates.description: Roll-up counts over the evaluated claims.

by_liveness.description: Count of claims per liveness class.

by_state.description: Count of claims per lifecycle state.

armed_stops.description: Number of claims carrying an armed stop.

blind_sources.description: The probe sources that could not be read this tick (one per COULD-NOT-CHECK claim), each naming the reason and claim key. Empty when every claim was read cleanly.
